chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kindi from more than one of his companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Zakariyya al-Naqqaaz from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
I heard him saying: The people became, after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family),
of the status of the one who followed Harun (peace be upon him) and the one who followed the calf.
And indeed Abu Bakr called, so Ali (peace be upon him) refused except for the Quran.
And indeed Umar called, so Ali (peace be upon him) refused except for the Quran.
And indeed Uthman called, so Ali (peace be upon him) refused except for the Quran.
And indeed there is no one who calls for the emergence of the Dajjal except that he will find someone who pledges allegiance to him.
And whoever raises a banner of misguidance, its owner is a tyrant.
ai.seo_question: What did Ali (peace be upon him) refuse to give except the Quran when called by the first three Caliphs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi employs the dual imagery of the Golden Calf and Harun to critique the post-Prophetic era, distinguishing between the majority who accepted political authority (Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman) and Ali (AS), who withheld allegiance until the Quran was fully implemented. In Shia scholarship, this 'refusal except for the Quran' highlights Ali's prioritization of divine text over immediate political consolidation, framing the subsequent caliphs as followers of a deviation akin to the calf-worshippers. The conclusion links this historical misguidance to the eschatological Dajjal, suggesting that any leader raising a 'banner of misguidance' embodies the archetype of the Taghut.
